doc_summary: LinuxArena is a large AI-control setting of 20 live multi-service production environments with 1,667 main tasks and 185 side tasks. It validates the setting through sabotage and monitor evaluations and releases LaStraj, a human-crafted attack dataset that evades monitors better than model-generated attacks.

items.claim: In a setup, make legitimate work and the target (harmful) behavior require overlapping access and resources instead of a separable attack surface, because then the opportunity for the behavior arises naturally inside ordinary work and is not signposted by the scenario.
items.quote: LinuxArena’s key property is that legitimate engineering work and sabotage require overlapping access. Main tasks depend on the same network access, service interactions, and live state that an attacker would use.

items.claim: In a setup, avoid giving the agent knowledge it could not naturally have (omniscience) and insert exploration steps so its actions look earned, because unearned knowledge is unrealistic and makes the transcript distinguishable.
items.quote: it is easy to create attack trajectories where the attacker is omniscient, i.e. can exploit detailed knowledge of the environment without having to explore relevant files or configurations (for example, knowing unexpected default values of function arguments).

items.claim: The paper distrusts synthetic placeholder data as an eval-awareness tell, noting a capable model might infer it is in an evaluation, while stating there is no current evidence of this.
items.quote: our environments use synthetic placeholder data rather than real production data. A sufficiently capable model might notice this and infer that it is operating in an evaluation, though we have no evidence this is currently happening.

items.claim: Prefers real-world-like multi-service stateful environments with application-specific codebases over generic or simple settings because simple settings make behavior easy to detect for reasons that do not transfer to deployment.
items.quote: a setting that is too simple may make sabotage easy to detect for reasons that do not transfer to deployment, while a setting with too little task diversity may yield narrow or noisy conclusions.

items.claim: Embedding the target behavior within legitimate main task work creates plausible deniability, which makes it harder for observers to flag; a realistic scenario hides the target behavior in plausible cover.
items.quote: All of these failure modes are highly amplified when the attack is integrated with legitimate main task work, since this creates the plausible deniability that leads to the monitor dismissing or completely passing over suspicious behavior.

items.claim: Prefers stress-testing against strong human-crafted adversaries over relying on model-generated attacks, because model elicitation underestimates the real threat and overestimates safety.
items.quote: A persistent challenge in AI control research is the lack of a strong attacker. Using only current-model attacks underestimates a future misaligned agent and overestimates safety.

items.claim: Rules out the null explanation that the behavior is infeasible before interpreting low rates, by measuring raw capability separately from stealth.
items.quote: If side tasks are intrinsically hard, low sabotage rates in § 5.2 could just mean the attacker couldn’t do the task, not that the monitor caught it. We need to rule this out.

items.claim: Explicitly flags realism deviations and their direction of bias (attacker-favorable, lower-bound safety) instead of claiming the setting matches deployment, because results may not transfer.
items.quote: this is attacker-favorable: it removes safety layers a real deployment would have, so our safety estimates are a lower bound, but our results may not transfer directly to settings with these intermediaries.

items.claim: Holds out part of the environments to reduce training-data contamination, a concern relevant to the model recognising the scenarios.
items.quote: We release 10 of the 20 environments publicly and withhold the remaining 10 to reduce the risk of training data contamination.

items.claim: Plans harder, longer tasks and richer protocols (agentic monitoring, trusted editing) as models grow more capable.
items.quote: As models handle longer, more complex engineering work, control evaluations need harder tasks. Harder tasks also provide richer attacker cover. We plan to expand LinuxArena with additional environments and more challenging main tasks.
